notice: RN bank batch 122: Hematologic and oncologic case studies: febrile neutropenia, tumor lysis, DIC and massive PE. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate follow-up.

rationale.correct: Fever, tachycardia, low blood pressure and raised lactate in a neutropenic client is sepsis until proven otherwise.

perOption.r1: Fever in neutropenia is an emergency; acetaminophen may mask a higher fever.
perOption.r4: Neutropenic clients show little inflammation; faint redness can be a serious infection.
perOption.r5: Low but not the immediate threat.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) = WBC x percentage of neutrophils (segs + bands). Using the results, calculate the ANC. Record your answer as cells/mm3, as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 0.9 x 10^3 = 900 cells/mm3; 900 x 0.12 = 108 cells/mm3. An ANC below 500 is severe neutropenia; below 100 is profound.
references: Laboratory reference ranges as used in common NCLEX review texts; follow the facility's ranges
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client is most at risk for {{b1}}. The most important goal in the first hour is {{b2}}.

options.text: blood cultures and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 60 minutes
waiting for the culture results before antibiotics
a chest x-ray before any treatment

rationale.correct: Antibiotics within the hour are the priority in febrile neutropenia.

perOption.b1:b: Platelets 88,000 are not the immediate threat.
perOption.b2:a: Delay increases death in febrile neutropenia.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: For each area, select the actions the plan should include.

options.text: Blood cultures from the port and a peripheral vein
Delay cultures until the fever reaches 39 C
30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension and lactate
A rectal temperature to confirm the fever
Private room and strict hand hygiene
Fresh flowers and fruit at the bedside

rationale.correct: Culture from line and periphery, antibiotics and fluids now, and protect from new infection.

perOption.b: Look for a source even without symptoms.
perOption.f: Rectal routes are avoided in neutropenia.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Cultures x2. Cefepime 2 g IV. Lactated Ringer's 30 mL/kg. Neutropenic precautions. Filgrastim daily.

questions.stem: The client is admitted to the oncology unit. Which tasks can the RN delegate to the UAP? Select all that apply.

options.text: Helping with oral care using a soft brush
Reporting a temperature above 38 C at once
Assessing the port site for spreading redness and pain
Teaching the family about neutropenic precautions at home
Giving the first filgrastim injection under the RN's watch

rationale.correct: UAPs measure, help with hygiene and report; assessing, teaching and medicines stay with licensed staff.

perOption.f: Medication administration cannot go to UAPs.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

exhibits.title: Day 1
exhibits.body: Blood pressure 118/70 after fluids. Lactate 1.4. Port culture pending.

questions.stem: On day 4 of filgrastim, for each finding, indicate whether it shows the expected response or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Aching in the lower back and hips
Left upper abdominal pain spreading to the shoulder
New shortness of breath with crackles

rationale.correct: Neutrophils recovered; left upper quadrant pain or breathlessness on filgrastim must be reported.

perOption.r3:c1: Bone pain is common as the marrow expands.
perOption.r3:c2: Bone pain is common as the marrow expands.

questions.stem: 15 minutes into the first unit of red cells, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the IV open with 0.9% sodium chloride using new tubing
Notify the provider and blood bank
Send the bag, tubing and a blood sample to the blood bank
Slow the transfusion and give diphenhydramine before continuing
Flush the remaining blood in the tubing into the client

rationale.correct: Fever, back pain and hypotension early in a transfusion is a hemolytic reaction: stop and investigate.

perOption.e: Fever and back pain are not a mild allergic reaction.
perOption.f: Gives more of the incompatible blood.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
